title: Global Head of Sustainability, Life Sciences and Chemicals Multinational ( SINGAPORE )
Data Specialist (Environmental/Shipping)
description:
Angle Recruitment has partnered with a well established liner and bulk shipping group to find an Environmental Data Specialist who can bring order to how it collects, measures and reports its impact.
  
  
Like every shipowner, the business has to report its carbon emissions, waste and water use. It burns fuel at sea, uses electricity ashore, sends crew and staff around the world, and buys goods and services from hundreds of suppliers. The rules for reporting all this are clear. The data behind it is not. Some figures come from systems, some from spreadsheets, and some from a vessel emailing numbers to the office. Each office does it a little differently, so the totals are hard to trust.
  
  
Your job is to fix that, and make sure it stays fixed.
  
  
You'll sit in Finance, reporting to the Finance Controller, because the priority is numbers that stand up to an auditor. You'll work closely with a small sustainability team of four, two on the fleet side and two in corporate, who know the business and the targets. Most of your focus will be on the liner business, with some support for the bulk side.
  
  
**In practice, you will:**  
Set the rules.
  
  
Turn group data policy into a practical way of working, with clear owners, controls and the evidence an auditor will ask for.
  
  
Find the gaps.
  
  
Map where every piece of carbon, waste and water data comes from, and spot the duplication, risks and manual workarounds.
  
  
Check the numbers.
  
  
Test data from across the business, spot what doesn't add up, and explain why.
  
  
Deliver the tools.
  
  
Build the case for practical tools and automation, then implement them within the systems that exist today.
  
  
Crack Scope 3.
  
  
Build a sensible approach to supplier, travel and crewing data, including business travel emissions and offsetting.
  
  
Make it stick.
  
  
Write clear guides and train the people who supply the data, so the process runs long after the two years are up.
  
  
You'll bring hands on experience managing Scope 1 and 2 inventories under the GHG Protocol, and a good eye for whether data is clean. You'll have designed data processes and controls that held up to review, ideally with some exposure to Scope 3 and external assurance. Shipping knowledge is useful but not essential. The client is open to someone slightly earlier in their career, as long as the carbon accounting and data quality skills are genuinely there.
  
  
In return, you'll get a clear brief, real influence across the business, and a competitive package. It's two years to build something that lasts.
  
  
Global Maritime Talent Experts
  
  
Angle Recruitment is a global company that specialises in maritime recruitment and executive search. With our extensive industry expertise and commitment to excellence, we combine traditional values with state-of-the-art technology to deliver exceptional recruitment solutions. Our goal is to establish ourselves as the trusted partner for maritime professionals and organisations seeking top-tier talent. Headquartered in Singapore, one of the world's largest shipping and commodity trading hubs, Angle Recruitment is strategically positioned to serve the global maritime community.

title: Research Fellow (Environmental Sciences)
description:
The Asian School of the Environment (ASE) at Nanyang Technological University is an interdisciplinary school that aims to be a world leader in environmental research focused on Asian environmental challenges. The ASE integrates earth and environmental life science, ecology, engineering and technology, human ecology, humanities, and the social sciences to address key issues of the environment and sustainability. For more details, please view https://www.ntu.edu.sg/ase .

  

The Wetland Carbon Lab at NTU’s Asian School of the Environment (ASE) focuses on understanding the role of wetlands and aquatic ecosystems, including mangroves peatlands, and streams, as natural climate solutions. The lab integrates field-based experiments, high-frequency sensor networks, stable isotope approaches, and modelling to study water, carbon, nitrogen, and energy fluxes and greenhouse gas emissions across ecosystems and watersheds.

We are seeking a highly motivated Research Fellow to lead eddy covariance data analysis for our greenhouse gas flux research in Southeast Asian wetlands. The position supports NTU’s mission to advance solution-oriented environmental research and contributes to climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies.

**Key Responsibilities:**

  

* Responsible for regular quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) of eddy covariance and supporting meteorological data, and for producing monthly data reports.
* Improve, standardize, and automate EC pre- and post-processing workflows (e.g. flux calculation, filtering, gap-filling, flux partitioning, uncertainty estimation), ensuring rigorous documentation and reproducibility.
* Prepare and contribute to peer-reviewed publications, research proposals, technical reports, and internal technical notes, and present findings at scientific meetings.
Contribute to the development of a Southeast Asian flux tower network, including data harmonization and partner engagement.  

**Job Requirements:**

  

* PhD in Environmental Science, Atmospheric Science, Micrometeorology, Biogeochemistry, Ecology, or a closely related field
* Strong experience in eddy covariance measurements of greenhouse gas (CO2, CH4) and energy fluxes.
* In-depth knowledge of eddy covariance theory and instrumentation, and of standard processing software.
* Analytical and modelling skills with R or Python; experience building automated, reproducible data pipelines.
* Excellent scientific communication and interpersonal skills
Proactive, independent, and team-oriented  

  

ASE seeks a diverse and inclusive workforce and is committed to equality of opportunity. We welcome applications from all and recruit based on merit, regardless of age, race, gender, religion, marital status and family responsibilities, or disability.

  

We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.
